Importing modules¶

The import system finds a module by name. It first looks at the cache described in the module cache, and then walks the search path. Details are in the language reference.

Importing is one of the first things a program does, so its cost adds to start-up time. The rest of this page explains where the time goes and how to look at it, with examples you can run in a terminal.

Module search path¶

When a module named spam is imported, the interpreter searches a list of directories. This paragraph sits in a section whose id contains the word search and must be kept.

import sys

def show():
    for entry in sys.path:
        print(entry)


show()

A makefile keeps its tabs:

build:
	cc -O2 -o app main.c
	strip app

The module cache¶

Modules that were imported already are kept in a table, so a second import of the same name costs almost nothing.

NameMeaning
sys.modulesModules already loaded
sys.pathWhere to look for new ones
  • Clearing the table forces a fresh import.
  • Entries may be replaced while a program runs.
